images.title: The cross net: opposite faces
images.purpose: Shows the cross shaped net of a cube with each pair of opposite faces in the same colour.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. One cross shaped net of 6 equal squares in the centre.
images.exact_structure: A column of 4 equal squares, labelled from top to bottom 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D' in the centre of each, and 2 more equal squares 'L' and 'R' attached on the left and right of 'B': 6 squares in a cross, thin dark outlines, fold lines between squares drawn as thin dashed grey lines (5 fold lines). Colours: B and D teal #0072B2, A and C amber #E69F00, L and R green #009E73. Under the net, small grey text: 'B is the bottom'. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Squares of the same colour become opposite faces of the cube.
images.description: Shows the cross shaped net of a cube with each pair of opposite faces in the same colour.
images.context: Concept T7.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Fold with B as bottom: A, C, L, R are walls, D is the lid. Opposite pairs: B and D, A and C, L and R.

image_decisions.why: A net is a flat picture of a solid; seeing the cross with its opposite pairs coloured is the concept.
